findings.description: Statement says the validator matches 'the rules TinyHttpd's parser applies', but TinyHttpd RequestParser also rejects (400) any raw request-target char <= 0x20 (space, controls), 0x7F (DEL) and '#'. AC-1 only lists chars above U+007F and NUL, so a validator built to the ACs accepts '/a b' or '/a\u0001' that TinyHttpd rejects; the in-memory/servlet adapters would diverge from TinyHttpd, against D-052 'on every adapter, matching TinyHttpd'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC-1: a raw space, a raw control char U+0001..U+001F, U+007F and '#' are rejected; or drop the 'matching TinyHttpd' clause and state the enumerated list is the full rule set.

findings.description: The lookup contract says 'the request path' without saying raw (not percent-decoded). TinyHttpd exposes both requestUri (raw) and path (already decoded AND with empty segments collapsed by PercentCodec.decodePath). An adapter passing the decoded path would double-decode (breaking D-051: '%252e' -> '.') and lose '//' (breaking the strict default of FR-ROUTE-005 AC-4). Only FR-ROUTE-005's 'decoding each segment exactly once' implies raw input.
findings.suggested_fix: State in IR-ROUTE-004 (and CON-ROUTE-001 AC-4) that lookup takes the raw, undecoded path as received in the request target; add an AC: lookup('GET','/files/%252e') yields name='%2e'.

findings.description: Lookup preconditions are undefined: (a) a path the validator would reject (e.g. '/a%zz') passed to lookup — there is no result variant (FR-ROUTE-004 AC-3) and no stated behaviour (throw? no match?); (b) upgrade flag true with a non-GET token; (c) lookup before freeze and registration after freeze. Implementers will choose differently and wave 3/4 depend on it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add ACs: invalid path -> IllegalArgumentException (or defined result); upgrade flag ignored unless token is GET; registration after freeze throws IllegalStateException; lookup requires (or does not require) a prior freeze.

findings.description: FR-ROUTE-002 lets any Method/MethodSet be registered with route kind WebSocket, but the design treats a WebSocket route as GET only (upgrade only on GET; Allow counts it as GET). A WebSocket registration under POST is undefined. Also 'not part of any public RestApp API in wave 2' is vacuous (RestApp does not exist in wave 2) so the 'internal hook' part of D-391 is not actually verified.
findings.suggested_fix: State that a WebSocket registration takes no method (implicitly GET) or that a non-GET WebSocket registration is a configuration error; replace the RestApp clause with a checkable one (e.g. hook is package-private / not on the public router signature, or a named internal method).

findings.description: Wave decision 'Markers' says wave 2 documents 'the decided routing semantics above' — that includes per-method priority (DELETE /users/me -> DELETE /users/:id), pattern validation (empty/repeated variable names, empty segment), policy-normalised conflicts, exact case-sensitive method tokens and the upgrade-flag header rule. AC-1 lists only path-form switches, TRACE/CONNECT, Allow rule and result order, so these decided semantics can be omitted from docs/api/routing.md while AC-1 passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend AC-1 to list per-method priority with the Express example, pattern validation errors, normalised conflict detection, method-token case sensitivity and the upgrade-flag rule (and the GET/HEAD 426 residual).

findings.description: 'actual method' is a D-390 field never defined in the SRS; FR-ROUTE-011 AC-1 fixes it to GET for automatic HEAD. Without a definition it is unclear whether 'actual method' means the request method or the matched registration's method (relevant for MethodSet registrations), and readers may take it as pre-deciding the wave 3 (미확정) req.method() value.
findings.suggested_fix: Define 'actual method' in IR-ROUTE-004 (e.g. the member of the registration's method set that matched; GET under automatic HEAD) and note it does not decide req.method() (D-398).

findings.description: AC-3 checks only non-static methods, yet claims 'so Method.GET.delete() does not compile'. In Java a static method is callable through an instance, so a static Method.delete() would make Method.GET.delete() compile while AC-3 passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Also require that Method has no static method named after an HTTP method other than get(), or add a compile-negative check.

findings.description: AC-4 says Allow 'contains' GET, HEAD, POST, OPTIONS; the rule gives an exact set, so an Allow with extra methods would pass.
Statement 'returning path parameter values as decoded once and otherwise as received' is vague; the wave decision means values are never case-folded or slash-normalised by policies.
findings.suggested_fix: Rephrase: parameter values are the segment decoded once, never case-folded or otherwise altered by any policy.

findings.description: 'recognised, routable method' is undefined in the statement (means a Method constant that is not a disabled TRACE/CONNECT).
findings.suggested_fix: Spell it out or reference FR-ROUTE-013/014.

findings.description: Nullability AC names no verification mechanism and covers only 'router types', not the public Method/MethodSet API.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify via @NullMarked package-info (or reflection) plus the Kotlin test compiling without platform types; include Method and MethodSet.

findings.description: If the iteration accessor exposes an Iterator/Iterable/Set, removal through it would break immutability yet AC-4 (no constructor/mutator, final fields) still passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: any exposed iterator/collection is unmodifiable (remove throws UnsupportedOperationException).

findings.description: Edge of trailing-slash ignoring on the root pattern '/' (stripping the only slash) is unspecified.
findings.suggested_fix: State that '/' is never stripped to empty.

findings.description: CLAUDE.md requires an Express correspondence for each API in docs/api; AC-2 asks only for Java and Kotlin examples of the accessors.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the Express counterpart (or 'no Express equivalent') next to the accessors.

findings.description: D-067's clause that the policy governs origin-/absolute-form CONNECT on the TinyHttpd adapter has no AC and is only in Rationale; fine to defer to wave 3, but it should be carried explicitly so it is not lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Mention it in Out of Scope / carried-into-wave-3 list.
